subject: InsightLane concession ask — gating, release window, and cost trade-offs
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: InsightLane concession ask — gating, release window, and cost trade-offs

Team —

Quick context: InsightLane is on a tight procurement timeline (Procurement sign-off by 6/18) and is asking us to commit to two items as part of their SOW: an audit/trace export for tenant-scoped logs and a configurable retention TTL for exported traces. They want the features gated into a short release window (end of June) as a condition of the pilot payment. Ben has the business case below.

Ask: I need product/eng to confirm scope, an estimate for engineering effort (rough t-shirt), and whether we can offer a short-term alternative (e.g., workaround using current exports + manual redaction) if we cannot ship by their deadline. Please reply with what you need from procurement/legal to scope the work.

Attachments: InsightLane_MAP_v2.xlsx (pilot commercial terms), SOW-draft-InsightLane.pdf

High-level asks from customer:
- Tenant-scoped audit export (CSV/JSON) filtered by org-id
- Retention TTL on exported artifacts (configurable per-tenant)
- Evidence for SOC2 traceability for the audit path

Impact: this is a ~ $450k ARR commitment if we can hit pilot acceptance. If we miss, risk of rolling to next quarter and potential discount pressure.

Thanks — will consolidate answers for procurement.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InsightLane concession ask — gating, release window, and cost trade-offs

+1 to urgency — adding the commercial context: InsightLane will run a 6-week pilot across three internal teams. They will pay pilot fees upon acceptance, then convert to a 12-month contract if the pilot meets their security gating. Procurement is explicit: no acceptance without tenant-level audit exports and retention controls.

Practical notes:
- They are fine with a narrow initial export schema (timestamp, request_id, org_id, route, model, user_agent, token_count) — not asking for full payloads.
- Their security lead (Priya Shah) expects an export job UI and API, not only a support ticket flow.

Workaround possibility: If engineering can't ship by 6/18, Procurement will accept a documented interim SOP plus a one-off data delivery cadence for the pilot (e.g., weekly exports delivered via secure SFTP). That reduces near-term liability but weakens positioning for enterprise.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InsightLane concession ask — gating, release window, and cost trade-offs

Thanks for the context — I did a quick pass with the infra team this afternoon. Notes:

1) Tenant-scoped export: doable as an export job that filters by tenant_id. We can reuse existing export plumbing (export service + S3-compatible sink) but need work in two areas: filtering at the routing layer (small), and exporting the enriched trace metadata (moderate). Rough estimate: 2 engineers x 3 weeks to deliver an MVP (export API + UI to schedule/run jobs).

2) Retention TTL per-export: this is mostly a policy/metadata flag that the export runner can honor. Small effort: 1 engineer x 1 week to wire up TTL param and configurable retention enforcement on the export worker.

3) Compliance evidence: SOC2 evidence will require traceability for who requested exports + immutable audit entries. This touches our audit log path and may require product review. Rough estimate: 1 engineer x 2 weeks + product/design to define required audit records.

Given the sums above, earliest realistic completion for a minimal acceptable feature set is ~4–5 weeks (target mid-July). If we compress and allocate a short project team (2FE, 1BE, 1PM) and prioritize, we could potentially hit late-June but would be a high-risk sprint.

Questions for product/legal/procurement:
- What exact audit fields does InsightLane require for SOC2 evidence? (e.g., requester identity, timestamp, export checksum)
- Do we need encrypted-at-rest export artifacts with customer-managed keys (they asked about KMS but didn't insist)?

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InsightLane concession ask — gating, release window, and cost trade-offs

Product note: we need to treat this as a gated, limited-scope feature request. If we greenlight, propose the following approach to minimize long-term cost and risk:

- Ship an "Export Jobs" MVP (tenant filter + TTL + export schema) behind a feature flag and mark as experimental for the InsightLane pilot only.
- Provide a documented interim SOP (SFTP weekly exports) as a fallback until the feature is GA.
- Agree to an explicit deprecation/GA path: experimental for 3 months, then review usage before promoting to GA.

Requirements from Sales/Legal:
- Written confirmation from InsightLane that they accept an "experimental" feature for pilot acceptance (we need to capture this in the SOW).
- Clarity on KMS requirement — if they insist on CCKM integration, that increases scope considerably.

If we adopt the experimental gating approach, we can commit to a late-June limited rollout (feature-flagged, single-tenant exposure) provided we allocate a small cross-functional team and freeze scope to the export schema above.

—PrIyom
PrIyom Das
Product Manager, Observability & Compliance
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InsightLane concession ask — gating, release window, and cost trade-offs

Appreciate the fast turn. Summary and next steps:

1) Product/Eng ask accepted: build Export Jobs MVP (tenant filter + TTL + export schema) behind a feature flag as experimental for InsightLane pilot. Target: feature-flagged rollout to InsightLane by 2027-06-28, with a risk caveat that GA is not yet promised.

2) Resource plan: Jonas to propose a short project team by EOD Monday (2 FE, 1 BE, 1 PM). PrIyom to draft the experimental gating language for the SOW.

3) Sales/legal: Ben to secure written acknowledgement from InsightLane that an experimental, feature-flagged export will satisfy pilot acceptance for the terms in InsightLane_MAP_v2.xlsx. If KMS is required, that will be a separate scoped addendum.

4) Interim fallback: Weekly SFTP exports until the feature is available — Ben, please confirm whether InsightLane can accept this if needed.

I'll keep procurement looped. Thanks everyone — I'll create a short project doc and add the Drive link (see related_links) and update HubSpot (deal IL-DEAL-8473).

—Monica
